sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup
sections.what: Imports the test tools and the calibration functions the tests use.
sections.why: Gives the tests access to the calibration functions.

sections.name: rng
sections.title: Seeded random generator
sections.what: Creates a random number source that gives the same sequence each time for the same seed.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the synthetic test data identical on every run.
sections.watch_out: Changing the arithmetic in this generator changes every synthetic test value.

sections.name: calibration: isotonic map
sections.title: Isotonic map tests
sections.what: Checks that the fitted correction never decreases, gives the expected step values, maps new inputs correctly, and rejects empty input. Checks that a deliberately miscalibrated model passes the gate after correction on held-out data.
sections.why: Likely reason: the correction exists to fix a known bias, so the test confirms that it does.
sections.watch_out: The fix test relies on large samples. Smaller samples could fail the gate from noise alone.

sections.name: calibration: buckets and gate
sections.title: Buckets and gate behaviour
sections.what: Checks that ten buckets of width 0.1 are built with correct counts, that empty buckets have no error value, that the gate skips small buckets, and that a stricter minimum makes the gate fail.
sections.why: Likely reason: the gate should not judge a bucket that has too few examples.
sections.watch_out: The minimum count per bucket controls how strict the gate is.

sections.name: gate power (calibration)
sections.title: Gate power and normal values
sections.what: Checks known values of the normal distribution. Checks that clustered samples have a larger standard error than independent ones, that certain predictions have zero error, and that too few samples give an empty result that passes.
sections.why: Likely reason: prevents the gate from being overconfident when several predictions come from one match.
sections.watch_out: Cluster labels must identify the match. If they do not, the error is understated.

summary: Checks the basic calibration tools on small synthetic examples: a stepwise correction map, reliability buckets, a calibration gate, and a power calculation for how well the gate can detect error.
purpose: Proves that the calibration helpers behave as intended before they are used on real data.
why: Likely reason: the calibration gate is only useful if its building blocks are proven on known cases.
how: Creates a seeded random source, then checks the isotonic fit on a small list, fits a correction to noisy data and checks that held-out buckets pass. Checks bucket building, empty buckets, the normal distribution values, the effect of clustering on error, and the skipping of small buckets.
inputs: Synthetic samples generated inside the test file.
risks: Results depend on the random generator staying the same. The large 20,000-sample tests can be slow.
debug: If the isotonic checks fail, look at how violating neighbours are pooled. If power numbers drift, compare the standard error formula inputs.
